newsitem.title: EU: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, DEC 16-SUNDAY, DEC 22 (PAGE 1/4 - HIGHLIGHTS).
newsitem.headline: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, DEC 16-SUNDAY, DEC 22 (PAGE 1/4 - HIGHLIGHTS).

text.p: Reuter EC Report Weekly Diary.
HIGHLIGHTS

WASHINGTON - U.S. President Bill Clinton hosts biannual U.S.-EU summit (Monday); dicussions focus on Bosnia; Central Europe; the Middle East; review of the progress made on the so-called new transatlantic agenda.
BRUSSELS - EU farm ministers meet (Monday-Tuesday); discussions focus on the current status of the beef market.
BRUSSELS - European Commissioner Fischler holds news conference on BSE (mad cow disease).
BRUSSELS - EU culture ministers meet (Monday); progress report on television without frontiers directive.

BRUSSELS - European Commission hosts conference on "Moving towards the Euro - Strategies and practical solutions for a competitive advantage" (Monday-Tuesday); European Commissioner de Silguy attends.
BRUSSELS - NATO defence ministers meet (Tuesday-Wednesday); discussions focus on reform of the alliance and future relations with Russia.
BRUSSELS - Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo and State Secretary Michiel Patijn hold joint news conference on the Dutch presidency's work programme (Wednesday).
BRUSSELS - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (Wednesday).

BRUSSELS - Economic and Social Committee holds plenary session (Wednesday-Thursday); European Commissioner Fischler speaks on "Implications for the CAP of enlargement to countries of central and eastern Europe" (Wednesday).
BRUSSELS - EU fisheries ministers meet (Thursday-Friday); discussions focus on 1997 fish catch quotas.
LUXEMBOURG - Executive committee of Schengen group on free movement of people meets at ministerial level under Luxembourg presidency (Thursday). European Commissioner Monti attends.
MONDAY, DECEMBER 16

WASHINGTON - U.S. President Bill Clinton hosts biannual U.S.-EU summit (1100/0400 GMT). Main discussions focus on Bosnia; Central Europe; the Middle East; review of the progress made on the so-called new transatlantic agenda which aims to promote peace and stability across the globe; confronting the new challenges of transnational crime; fostering a healthier environment; and promoting the free flow of trade and investment. Participants include: Irish Prime Minister John Bruton, European Commission President Jacques Santer and European Commissioner Brittan.
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Farm Council (1500/1400 GMT) (and Tuesday).
Agenda includes:
- Modification of the support regime to arable producers (sanctions regime).
- Commission report on the application of individual producer limits under the annual suckler cows and ewes premium schemes.
- Conference of EU intervention agency directors.
- Community policy programme and action in environment and sustainable development.
- Commission communication on the nomination of the vice president and president of the Community plant variety office.
- Proposal for decision on the ban on specified risk material for TSEs (transmissible spongiform encephalopathies) in human food and animal feed production.
- State of work on BSE (mad cow disease).
- Proposal for directive modifying directive 91/629/EEC on minimum standards for the protection of calves.
- Proposal for decision on the conclusion of a veterinary and plant health equivalence accord with New Zealand.
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Culture Council (1000/0900 GMT).
Agenda includes:
- Proposal for a decision on Community support programme in the field of books and reading (ARIANE).
- Proposal for a decision on Community action programme in the field of cultural heritage (RAPHAEL).
- Draft resolution on the integration of cultural aspects into Community actions.
- European Cities of Culture:
* Cities of culture for the year 2000;
* Oral information from the Commission on a proposal for the period following the year 2000;
* Application from the city of Plovdiv (Bulgaria) as European Cultural Month 1999.
- Commission presentation on the current situation on book pricing - followed by a debate.
- Commission information on "Music in Europe".
- Progress report on proposal for a directive amending Directive 89/552/EEC: "Television without frontiers".
- Progress report on the proposal for a Council decision on a European Guarantee Fund to promote cinema and television production.
- Development of new audiovisual services:
- Green paper on the protection of minors and human dignity in the audiovisual and information services - Presentation by the Commission and draft Council conclusions;

- Procedure for the provision of information in the field of technical standards and regulations - proposal for a directive amending for the third time Directive 83/189/EEC - exchange of views at the initiative of the French delegation.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Fischler holds news conference on BSE (mad cow disease) (1200/1100 GMT).

BRUSSELS - European Commission hosts conference on "Moving towards the Euro - Strategies and practical solutions for a competitive advantage" (0900/0800 GMT) (and Tuesday). Agenda includes: results of the Dublin European Council; which systems should be set up between the member states that join EMU and the rest?; stability pact; role of national central banks before and after the switch to the single currency; U.K. and the monetary union; strategic impact of EMU on European banking and the financial sector; European consumers and the euro; impact of the euro on mortgages and the advantages for consumers; producing coins and notes in euros and putting them in circulation; the role of European savings banks in the switch to the euro. Speakers include: European Commissioner de Silguy; Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt; German Finance State Secretary Juergen Stark; Belgian National Bank Governor Alfons Verplaetse. Venue: Hilton Hotel. Contact: EFMA (33) 1 47 42 52 72.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (1500/1400 GMT) Foreign Affairs;
Sub-Monetary - Commissioner de Silguy
attends;
Social Affairs - Commissioner Flynn
attends;
Regional Policy;
Environment;
Civil Liberties;
Budgetary Control;
Rules of Procedure;
Petitions;
Inquiry into Fraud in Transit.

BRUSSELS - European Film Companies Alliance (EFCA) holds news conference to discuss the audiovisual guarantee fund and to present the industry's arguments in favour of its establishment (1030/0930 GMT). Venue: International Press Centre (IPC). Contact: Heidi Lambert Communications (322) 732 5546.
BRUSSELS - Federation of Belgian Businesses holds conference on "The Internal Market: a new action plan" (0945/0845 GMT).
Agenda includes:
- (1010/0910 GMT) European Commissioner Monti gives address on "Internal Market: a springboard towards competitiveness, growth and employment".
- (1100/1000 GMT) DG XV Head of Unit John Farnell gives address on "Summary: impact and efficiency of the single market".
- (1120/1020 GMT) DG XV Director Thierry Stoll gives address on "Agenda for the future: how to improve the functioning of the internal market?".
Venue: FEB, 4 rue Ravenstein. Contact: Mrs Legrand, FEB (322) 515 0826.

BRUSSELS - European Environmental Network (EEN) holds conference on "Environmental regulations in central and eastern Europe" (0815/0715 GMT). Speakers include: UNICE Secretary General Zygmunt Tyszkiewicz; DG IA Head of Unit Marc Franco and Polish Ambassador to the EU Jan Truszczynski. Venue: Kredietbank, Havenlaan 2. Contact: Patrick De Bleser, EEN (322) 510 3231.

BRUSSELS - European Transport Safety Council (ETSC) holds conference on "Increasing survivability in aircraft accidents" (0930/0830 GMT). Speakers include: MEP Mark Watts. Venue: Dorint Hotel. Contact: ETSC (322) 230 4106.

LONDON - Information Society Observatory of the European Institute and the London School of Economics and Political Science holds conference on "Europeans in the information society" (0830/0730 GMT) (and Tuesday). Speakers include: European Commissioner Bangemann. Venue: The Old Theatre. Contact: Jonathan Barton (44) 171 955 6022.
LUXEMBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Please note EU Court of Justice closed for Christmas holidays until Monday, January 6.
TUESDAY, DECEMBER 17
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Farm Council (second of two days).
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner van den Broek attends EU-Czech Republic joint parliamentary committee.
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - NATO defence ministers meet (and Wednesday). Discussions focus on reform of the alliance and future relations with Russia.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - World Confederation of Labour (WCL) holds news conference on the outcome of the WTO meeting in Singapore (1100/1000 GMT). Venue: WCL Secretariat, 33 rue de Treves. Contact: WCL (322) 285 4714.
BRUSSELS - EP committee of inquiry into fraud in transit due to hear representatives of tobacco company Philip Morris Europe.

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime seminar on "The Dutch presidency of the EU council of ministers" (1315/1215 GMT). Speaker is Dutch Permanent Representative Ambassador Bernard Rudolf Bot. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.
WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 18

BRUSSELS - Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo and State Secretary Michiel Patijn hold joint news conference on the Dutch presidency's work programme (1600/1500 GMT). Venue: Justus Lipsius building, press room.
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (0900/0800 GMT).
Provisional agenda includes:
- State aids including Forges de Clabecq; Thomson Multimedia; German regional aid 1997-1999.
- Commissioner Van Miert communication on conditions imposed on second mobile phone operators.
- Commissioner Fischler communication on olive oil and olive sector; communication on the common market in tobacco.
- Commissioner Flynn communication on action against tobacco consumption.

- Commissioner Bjerregaard communication on marketing of genetically modified maize; communication on the introduction to the Community of furs and manufactured products from certain wild animal species.
- Commissioner Marin communication on the application of the generalised preferences system with Burma.
- Proposal for Council regulation on certain modes of applying an interim agreement with Slovenia.
- Commissioner Brittan communication on relations with Russia in the textile sector.

BRUSSELS - European Commission holds a multidisciplinary forum on electronic records (DLM) (to Friday). Speakers include Commission Secretary General David Williamson. Venue: Borschette Centre. Contact: Downtown Europe, (322) 732 3520.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (0900/0800 GMT) Agriculture;
Energy;

Legal Affairs;

Fisheries.
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC) holds plenary session (1430/1330 GMT) (and Thursday).
Agenda includes:
- Food additives other than colours and sweetners COM(96)303.
- (1500/1400 GMT) European Commissioner Fischler gives address on "Implications for the CAP of enlargement to countries of central and eastern Europe".
- Holding, movement and monitoring of products subjects to excise duty COM(96)548.
- Resale rights for the benefit of the author of an original work of art COM(96)97.
THURSDAY, DECEMBER 19
BRUSSELS - Fisheries Council (1000/0900 GMT) (and Friday).
Provisional agenda includes:
- Proposal for a Council regulation fixing, for certain fish stocks and groups of fish stocks, the total allowable catches for 1997 and certain conditions under which they may be caught.

- (possibly) Proposal for a Council regulation amending Council regulation (EEC) No. 3074/95 fixing, for certain fish stocks and groups of fish stocks, the total allowable catches for 1996 and certain conditions under which they may be caught.
- (Possibly) Proposal for a Council regulation laying down certain rules for the access to Community waters of research vessels for scientific purposes.
- (Possibly) Commission proposal on the financing of collection of scientific data.

- (Possibly) Proposal for a Council regulation (EC) amending regulation (EEC) No. 2847/93 establishing a control system applicable to the common fisheries policy (establishment of a Community catch-reporting data-base).
- (Possibly) Proposal for a Council decision on MAGP IV.
- Proposals for Council regulations
a) laying down, for 1997, certain measures for the conservation and management of fisheries resources applicable to vessels flying the flag of Norway;
b) allocating, for 1997, certain catch quotas between member states for vessels fishing in the Norwegian exclusive zone and the fishing zone around Jan Mayen.
- Proposals for Council regulations:
a) laying down, for 1997, certain measures for the conservation and management of fisheries resources applicable to vessels flying the flag of the Faroes;
b) allocating, for 1997, certain catch quotas between member states for vessels fishing in Faroese waters.
- Proposal for a Council regulation allocating, for 1997, Community catch quotas in Greenland waters.
- Proposal for Council regulation allocating, for 1997, certain catch quotas between member states for vessels fishing in Icelandic waters.
- Proposals for Council regulations:
a) laying down, for 1997, certain measures for the conservation and management of fisheries resources applicable to vessels flying the flag of Estonia;
b) allocating, for 1997, catch quotas between member states for vessels fishing in Estonian waters.
- Proposals for Council regulations:
a) laying down, for 1997, certain measures for the conservation and management of fisheries resources applicable to vessels flying the flag of Latvia;
b) allocating, for 1997, catch quotas between member states for vessels fishing in Latvian waters.
- Proposals for Council regulations
a) laying down, for 1997, certain measures for the conservation and management of fisheries resources applicable to vessels flying the flag of Lithuania;

b) allocating, for 1997, catch quotas between member states for vessels fishing in Lithuanian waters. - a) laying down, for 1997, certain measures for the conservation and management of fisheries resources applicable to vessels flying the flag of Poland;
b) allocating, for 1997, catch quotas between member states for vessels fishing in Polish waters.
- a) laying down, for 1997, certain measures for the conservation and management of fisheries resources applicable to vessels flying the flag of the Russian Federation;
b) allocating, for 1997, catch quotas between member states for vessels fishing in Russian waters.

- Proposal for Council regulation laying down, for 1997, certain conservation and management measures for fisheries resources in the regulatory area as defined in the Convention on future multilateral cooperation in the North West Atlantic Fisheries.

- Proposal for a Council regulation laying down, for 1997, certain measures for the conservation and management of fisheries resources applicable to vessels flying the flag of certain non-member countries in the 200-nautical-mile zone off the coast of the French Department of Guiana.
- (Possibly) NAFO: New STACFAC regulations.
- Proposals for Council decisions:
a) Authorising the Kingdom of Spain to extend the agreement on mutual fisheries relations with the Republic of South Africa;
b) Authorising the Portuguese Republic to extend the agreement on mutual fisheries relations with the Republic of South Africa.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission President Santer meets Brunei Sultan Sir Hassanal Bolkiah.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:

Transport;

BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC) holds plenary session (0900/0800 GMT) (second of two days).
Agenda includes:
- Common organisation of the market in raw tobacco COM(96)478.
- Specific measures in favour of cephalopod producers permanently based in the Canary Islands COM(96)528.
- XXVth report on competition plocy COM(96)126.

LUXEMBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - Executive committee of Schengen group on free movement of people meets at ministerial level under Luxembourg presidency (and Friday). The agreements with the five Nordic countries should be signed. Participants include: European Commissioner Monti. Venue: Kirchberg conference centre.
